comparisons.peer_topic: Consolidation criteria for agency vs. non-agency securitizations
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi does not consolidate U.S. agency-sponsored mortgage securitization entities as it lacks power to direct significant activities, whereas it consolidates certain non-agency entities only if it is the primary beneficiary with the power to direct significant activities or absorbs significant losses/benefits.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and C disclose consolidation policies for agency vs. non-agency mortgage securitizations based on power to direct activities. BAC consolidates agency trusts only when it holds substantially all securities, implying it lacks power to direct activities otherwise. Similarly, C states it does not consolidate U.S. agency-sponsored entities because it lacks the power to direct significant activities. Both firms consolidate non-agency or whole-loan trusts if they act as servicer (possessing power to direct) and hold significant interests.

sentences.text: The Corporation generally does not have the power to direct the most significant activities of a residential mortgage agency trust except in certain circumstances in which the Corporation holds substantially all of the issued securities and has the unilateral right to liquidate the trust.

The Corporation consolidates a whole-loan securitization trust if it has the power to direct the most significant activities and also holds securities issued by the trust or has other contractual arrangements, other than standard representations and warranties, that could potentially be significant to the trust.

Citi is not the primary beneficiary of its U.S. agency-sponsored mortgage securitization entities because Citigroup does not have the power to direct the activities of the VIEs that most significantly impact the entities' economic performance.
Therefore, Citi does not consolidate these U.S. agency-sponsored mortgage securitization entities.

In certain instances, the Company has (i) the power to direct the activities that most significantly impact the entities' economic performance and (ii) the obligation to either absorb losses or the right to receive benefits that could be potentially significant to its non-agency-sponsored mortgage securitization entities and, therefore, is the primary beneficiary and, thus, consolidates the VIE.

comparisons.peer_topic: Credit card securitization structure and accounting treatment
comparisons.peer_summary: Citigroup securitizes credit card receivables through non-recourse revolving trusts, specifically the Citibank Credit Card Master Trust and Citibank Omni Trust. Because Citigroup consolidates these entities as servicer and holds interests, the transferred receivables and associated third-party debt remain on its Consolidated Balance Sheet with no gain or loss recognized.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and C disclose consolidation of credit card securitization trusts. BAC includes credit cards as part of its whole-loan securitization trusts where it acts as servicer and holds significant interests, leading to consolidation. C explicitly consolidates its Credit Card Master Trust and Omni Trust because, as servicer, it has the power to direct significant activities and holds seller's interests/securities that expose it to potentially significant losses or benefits.

sentences.text: When the Corporation is the servicer of whole loans held in a securitization trust, including non-agency residential mortgages, home equity loans, credit cards, and other loans, the Corporation has the power to direct the most significant activities of the trust.

The Corporation consolidates a whole-loan securitization trust if it has the power to direct the most significant activities and also holds securities issued by the trust or has other contractual arrangements, other than standard representations and warranties, that could potentially be significant to the trust.
These trusts are consolidated entities because, as servicer, Citigroup has the power to direct the activities that most significantly impact the economic performance of the trusts.
Citigroup holds a seller's interest and certain securities issued by the trusts, which could result in exposure to potentially significant losses or benefits from the trusts.

comparisons.peer_summary: A VIE lacks characteristics of a voting interest entity and is consolidated if the firm holds variable interests giving it the power to direct significant activities and the obligation to absorb losses or right to receive significant benefits. Further details on VIEs are provided in Note 17.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS define consolidation criteria for Variable Interest Entities (VIEs). BAC consolidates VIEs (like whole-loan trusts) if it has the power to direct the most significant activities and holds securities/contractual arrangements that could be significant. GS consolidates VIEs if it has variable interests providing both the power to direct activities significantly impacting economic performance and the obligation to absorb losses or right to receive significant benefits. The criteria for consolidation (power + significant interest/loss exposure) are substantively the same, though GS explicitly defines the VIE framework while BAC applies it to specific trust types.

sentences.text: The Corporation consolidates a whole-loan securitization trust if it has the power to direct the most significant activities and also holds securities issued by the trust or has other contractual arrangements, other than standard representations and warranties, that could potentially be significant to the trust.

The firm has a controlling financial interest in a VIE when the firm has a variable interest or interests that provide it with (i) the power to direct the activities of the VIE that most significantly impact the VIE's economic performance and (ii) the obligation to absorb losses of the VIE or the right to receive benefits from the VIE that could potentially be significant to the VIE.

comparisons.peer_topic: Non-consolidation criteria for residential mortgage securitizations
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm does not consolidate residential mortgage securitizations, whether Firm-sponsored or third-party-sponsored, when it is not the servicer (and thus lacks power to direct significant activities) or does not hold a potentially significant beneficial interest in the trust.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM disclose that servicer status is key to consolidating residential mortgage securitizations. BAC states it generally does not have power to direct activities in agency trusts except when holding substantially all securities, but for whole-loan trusts (including non-agency residential mortgages), it consolidates if it is servicer and holds significant interests. JPM explicitly states it does not consolidate residential mortgage securitizations if it is not the servicer (and thus lacks power to direct activities) or does not hold a potentially significant beneficial interest.

sentences.text: When the Corporation is the servicer of whole loans held in a securitization trust, including non-agency residential mortgages, home equity loans, credit cards, and other loans, the Corporation has the power to direct the most significant activities of the trust.

The Corporation consolidates a whole-loan securitization trust if it has the power to direct the most significant activities and also holds securities issued by the trust or has other contractual arrangements, other than standard representations and warranties, that could potentially be significant to the trust.

The Firm does not consolidate residential mortgage securitizations (Firm-sponsored or third-party-sponsored) when it is not the servicer (and therefore does not have the power to direct the most significant activities of the trust) or does not hold a beneficial interest in the trust that could potentially be significant to the trust.

comparisons.peer_topic: Investment and Control Structure of Commercial Mortgage VIEs
comparisons.peer_summary: Treasury and CIO may invest in these securitizations. For these variable interest entities, the power to direct significant activities is generally held by the servicer or investors in a specified class of securities (controlling class), and the Firm generally does not retain an interest in the controlling class.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM describe the distribution of power in commercial mortgage securitization trusts. BAC states that power to direct significant activities in commercial mortgage trusts is typically held by the special servicer or the party holding specific subordinate securities with controlling rights. JPM similarly states that for commercial mortgage securitizations, the power to direct significant activities is generally held by the servicer or investors in a specified controlling class of securities. Both note that the reporting entity (BAC/JPM) generally does not hold the controlling interest that grants this power.

sentences.text: The power to direct the most significant activities of a commercial mortgage securitization trust is typically held by the special servicer or by the party holding specific subordinate securities which embody certain controlling rights.

For commercial mortgage securitizations the power to direct the significant activities of the VIE generally is held by the servicer or investors in a specified class of securities ("controlling class").
The Firm generally does not retain an interest in the controlling class in its sponsored commercial mortgage securitization transactions.

comparisons.peer_topic: Consolidation Criteria for Securitizations and CDOs
comparisons.peer_summary: For securitizations and CDOs, the Firm consolidates only if it acts as servicer or collateral manager (representing power to make significant economic decisions) or holds rights to replace the servicer/manager or require liquidation, provided it also holds a potentially significant interest.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and MS define servicing as the primary source of power to direct significant activities in securitizations, leading to consolidation if significant interests are held. BAC states that when it is the servicer of whole loans (including non-agency residential mortgages), it has the power to direct the most significant activities and consolidates if it also holds significant interests. MS states that servicing decisions represent the power to make the most significant economic decisions and that it consolidates securitizations where it acts as servicer and holds a potentially significant interest.

sentences.text: When the Corporation is the servicer of whole loans held in a securitization trust, including non-agency residential mortgages, home equity loans, credit cards, and other loans, the Corporation has the power to direct the most significant activities of the trust.

The Corporation consolidates a whole-loan securitization trust if it has the power to direct the most significant activities and also holds securities issued by the trust or has other contractual arrangements, other than standard representations and warranties, that could potentially be significant to the trust.
The Firm considers servicing or collateral management decisions as representing the power to make the most significant economic decisions in transactions such as securitizations or CDOs.

If the Firm serves as servicer or collateral manager, or has certain other rights described in the previous sentence, the Firm analyzes the interests in the VIE that it holds and consolidates only those VIEs for which it holds a potentially significant interest in the VIE.
